title: Cone calculation for a cofibrant coefficient section
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Give the category of unbounded cochain complexes of $B_n$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] the flat model structure of [lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model] for every $n$. Assume that for all $i\ge j$ extension of scalars $F_{ij}=B_j\otimes_{B_i}-$ and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] form a differential graded Quillen adjunction, with the ordinary tensor associators and units as the coherent composition isomorphisms. Let $\operatorname{Sect}$ be the category of strict sections of this diagram, with the projective differential graded model structure of [lem-coef-quillen-section-rectification]: an object is a family of complexes $Q_n$ with structure maps $B_n\otimes_{B_{n+1}}Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$ satisfying the composition identities, and weak equivalences and fibrations are the componentwise quasi-isomorphisms and fibrations. Let $Q$ be a cofibrant object of $\operatorname{Sect}$. Write $Q[1]$ for the componentwise shift, $Q[1]_n^k=Q_n^{k+1}$ with differential $-d$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $CQ=\operatorname{Cone}(1_Q)$ for the componentwise cone, $(CQ)_n^k=Q_n^{k+1}\oplus Q_n^k$ with differential $(x,y)\mapsto(-dx,x+dy)$ and the structure maps induced from those of $Q$; let $Q\to CQ$ be $y\mapsto(0,y)$. Then $Q\to CQ$ is a map of sections and a cofibration of $\operatorname{Sect}$, its cokernel is $Q[1]$, and $CQ$ is contractible by a contraction compatible with the structure maps; in particular $CQ\to0$ is a componentwise quasi-isomorphism, hence a weak equivalence.

source.place: Adic-stage paragraph before the inverse limit: explicit cone and suspension check for the projective section model.

proof.text: Write $s_{ij}:B_j\otimes_{B_i}Q_i\to Q_j$ for the structure maps. On the cone the map is $(x,y)\mapsto(s_{ij}x,s_{ij}y)$ under the tensor/direct-sum identifications. Since $s_{ij}$ commutes with $d$, it commutes with $(x,y)\mapsto(-dx,x+dy)$; also $d_C^2(x,y)=(0,-dx+dx)=0$. Applying the same two summand maps to a composable pair of transitions gives exactly the composition identity for $Q$ on each summand. Thus these are strict sections. The shift transition is $s_{ij}$ on the shifted terms and commutes with $-d$. Finally $d_C(0,y)=(0,dy)$ and $s_{ij}(0,y)=(0,s_{ij}y)$, so the inclusion $i:Q\to CQ$ is a map of sections.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, after reversing its two summands; direct verification for the given section transitions.

proof.text:
Take any trivial fibration $p:X\to Y$ in $\operatorname{Sect}$. In the dg model structure of [lem-coef-quillen-section-rectification], use the cofibration $0\to Q$ (the hypothesis that $Q$ is cofibrant) and $p$ in the stated Hom-complex compatibility axiom. The resulting map is
$$v:\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,X)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Y),\qquad u\longmapsto pu,$$
since the Hom complexes out of zero vanish. It is a trivial fibration in the projective model category of abelian-group complexes. Here a degree-$r$ element is a family $u_n^k:Q_n^k\to X_n^{k+r}$ commuting with all section transitions, and $\delta u=d_Xu-(-1)^ru d_Q$. These equations are the dg enrichment on complexes of sections, so lifting in this Hom complex retains the section compatibility.

source.place: Adic-stage normalized-system construction: agent-written Hom-complex lifting argument for its section model.

proof.text: Consider a commutative square with $i$ on the left and $p$ on the right, with top map $a:Q\to X$ and bottom map $b:CQ\to Y$, so $bi=pa$. Set $t_n^k(q)=b_n^{k-1}(q,0)$. The chain-map equation for $b$ gives $d_Yt+td_Q=pa$: indeed $d_Yb(q,0)=b(-dq,q)=-t(dq)+pa(q)$. The family $t$ commutes with the section transitions, and hence belongs to $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}^{-1}(Q,Y)$. By [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], with $R=\mathbf Z$ and $n=-1$, the map $S^0\hookrightarrow D^{-1}$ is a projective cofibration, where $D^{-1}$ has $\mathbf Z$ in degrees $-1,0$ and identity differential. Map $S^0$ to $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,X)$ by the closed element $a$, and $D^{-1}$ to $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Y)$ by $t$ in degree $-1$ and $pa$ in degree zero. The equation just checked makes a commutative square against the trivial fibration $v$ of step 2. Its lift supplies a compatible degree-$-1$ family $h$ with $ph=t$ and $\delta h=d_Xh+hd_Q=a$.

source.place: Adic-stage normalized-system construction: lifting against the projective cochain generator to obtain a section-compatible null-homotopy.

proof.text:
Define $l_n^k:(CQ)_n^k\to X_n^k$ by $l_n^k(x,y)=h_n^{k+1}(x)+a_n^k(y)$. Then
$$d_Xl(x,y)=(a(x)-h(dx))+a(dy)=l(-dx,x+dy),$$
so $l$ is a chain map. Both $h$ and $a$ commute with the transitions, so $l$ is a map of sections. We have $li=a$, and $pl(x,y)=t(x)+pa(y)=b(x,y)$ by additivity and the definitions of $t$ and $a$. Thus every square against any trivial fibration has a filler. The two weak factorization systems are generated by sets, and the (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) system stated in [lem-coef-quillen-section-rectification] characterizes its left class by precisely this lifting property. Therefore $i$ is a cofibration in the section model structure.

source.place: Adic-stage normalized-system construction: explicit filler and the stated weak-factorization-system characterization.

proof.text: The projection $\pi:CQ\to Q[1]$, $(x,y)\mapsto x$, commutes with transitions and satisfies $\pi d_C=-d_Q\pi$, so is a map of sections with $\pi i=0$. If $r:CQ\to Z$ is any map of sections with $ri=0$, then $r_n^k(x,y)=r_n^k(x,0)$. Define $\bar r_n^k(x)=r_n^k(x,0)$. The chain-map identity reads $d_Z\bar r(x)=r(-dx,x)=-\bar r(dx)$, and the transition identity follows by applying that for $r$ to $(x,0)$. Thus $\bar r:Q[1]\to Z$ is a map of sections and $r=\bar r\pi$. It is unique because $\pi_n^k(x,0)=x$. This is the cokernel universal property in the section category; no exactness of scalar extension is used.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, canonical projection onto the shift, with the cokernel universal property checked directly.

proof.text: Define $H_n^k:(CQ)_n^k\to(CQ)_n^{k-1}$ by $H(x,y)=(y,0)$. Every transition acts by the same $s_{ij}$ on the two summands, so $H_js_{ij}=s_{ij}H_i$. The two composites are $d_CH(x,y)=(-dy,y)$ and $Hd_C(x,y)=(x+dy,0)$; their sum is $(x,y)$. Hence $d_CH+Hd_C=1$ is a contraction compatible with every structure map. On the kernel of $d_C$ this identity is $z=d_CHz$, so the image of the preceding differential equals that kernel as sheaves, and every cohomology sheaf of $(CQ)_n$ vanishes. Consequently $CQ\to0$ is a componentwise quasi-isomorphism, and the componentwise weak-equivalence clause of [lem-coef-quillen-section-rectification] makes it a weak equivalence of sections.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone; explicit identity-cone contraction and its effect on cohomology, written out by the agent.
